BMO Capital Markets upgraded Ionis Pharmaceuticals
to outperform from market perform citing the rapid uptake of Tryngolza (olezarsen) for its second indication, reducing severe hypertriglyceridemia, which came in June.
The bank bumped its price target to $66 from $54 (~45% upside based on Wednesday's close).

Analyst David Lebowitz said that patients with acute pancreatitis are "clear candidates for Tryngolza, given a high AP recurrence rate and the limited efficacy of fibrates. Meanwhile, favorable payer dynamics could support strong and rapid uptake among high-risk patients."
In the long term, he added that Tryngolza will have an equal market share—and possibly more—with Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals'
Redemplo (plozasiran). Lebowitz sees more than $3B in peak revenue for Tryngolza.

He noted that for Tryngolza's other indication, reducing triglycerides in familial chylomicronemia syndrome, major pharmacy benefit managers such as Express Scripts have positioned the treatment ahead of Redemplo.

title: Ionis upgraded at BMO on Tryngolza adoption for severe hypertriglyceridemia
